input.question: Why are we able to cross our eyes and unable to do the opposite?
input.ground_truth: Some people can do just that. Otherwise, it just fucks with your brain trying to put two images from both eyes at different angles together. Crossing out eyes focuses on something in front of us. Making the eyes look in their own direction doesn't do us any good for survival, so the skill never really evolved

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why are we able to cross our eyes and unable to do the opposite?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your eyes are like two balloons on your face. You can make the two balloons move toward each other and cross, right? That’s easy because your eyes can turn inwards.

But if you try to make your eyes move away from each other as much as they can cross, you can’t. That’s because your eyes are held in place by muscles and skin, and they’re not made to move that way. It’s like your arms can only bend so much before they can’t go any farther. Your eyes can only move in certain directions, not the opposite way of crossing.

So, you can cross your eyes, but you can’t “uncross” them in the other direction because that’s not how your eyes are built!
